shared.commonMistake: CSS requirements look for the selector and declaration that affect the preview. Extra rules are fine, but styling the wrong class or writing the property outside the right rule will not complete the step.
shared.bestPractice: Start with the smallest {topic} rule that changes the preview, then adjust values once the target element clearly responds.
shared.semicolonCheck: Every CSS declaration ends with a semicolon

css-text-color.title: Color one clear target
css-text-color.summary: A class selector styles every element with that class. Start by changing one obvious preview target.
css-text-color.objective: Target .hero-title and give it a visible text color.
hints: A CSS rule has two parts: a selector that picks elements, and declarations that style them.
Select the title with .hero-title and set its color property.
`.hero-title { color: #1d4ed8; }`
checks: Hero title has a color declaration

css-card-background.title: Paint a component surface
css-card-background.summary: background-color changes the painted surface behind an element content area and padding.
css-card-background.objective: Target .preview-card and set a background-color so the cards become distinct blocks.
hints: Each card can get a surface color so it stands out from the page.
Target .preview-card and set background-color.
`.preview-card { background-color: #f8fafc; }`
checks: Preview cards have a background color

css-font-size.title: Scale the main heading
css-font-size.summary: font-size controls text scale. rem values are predictable because they are based on the root font size.
hints: Text size comes from one property, and rem units follow the reader's own settings.
Target .hero-title and set font-size to a larger value.
`.hero-title { font-size: 3rem; }`
checks: Hero title has a font size

css-font-weight.title: Strengthen important text
css-font-weight.summary: font-weight controls the weight of text. Numeric values such as 700 are useful in design systems.
hints: Bold is a weight, not a size. Numbers from 100 to 900 control how thick the letters are.
Target .stat-value and set font-weight to a heavy value.
`.stat-value { font-weight: 800; }`
checks: Stat value has a strong font weight

css-line-height.title: Make body copy easier to read
css-line-height.summary: line-height controls the vertical rhythm inside multi-line text.
css-line-height.objective: Set line-height on .intro-copy so the paragraph breathes.
hints: The space between lines makes long text easier to read.
Target .intro-copy and set line-height. Numbers without a unit scale with the font size.
`.intro-copy { line-height: 1.6; }`
checks: Intro copy has readable line height

css-text-align.title: Center the hero content
css-text-align.summary: text-align aligns inline content and text inside a block.
css-text-align.objective: Center the text inside .hero with text-align.
hints: Alignment is set on the container and applies to the text inside it.
Target .hero and set text-align.
`.hero { text-align: center; }`

css-badge-style.title: Style a small label
css-badge-style.summary: Small interface labels often use casing rules to separate metadata from body copy.
css-badge-style.objective: Target .badge and use text-transform to make the badge uppercase.
hints: CSS can change how text looks without changing the text in the HTML.
Target .badge and use text-transform.
`.badge { text-transform: uppercase; }`
checks: Badge text is transformed to uppercase

css-grouped-selectors.title: Share one declaration
css-grouped-selectors.summary: Selector lists let related elements share a declaration without duplicating rules.
css-grouped-selectors.objective: Use one grouped selector for .section-title and .card-title, then set their color.
hints: When two selectors need the same styles, one rule can target both.
List .section-title and .card-title separated by a comma, then add color.
`.section-title, .card-title { color: #334155; }`
checks: Section and card titles share one color rule

css-descendant-selector.title: Target list items in context
css-descendant-selector.summary: A descendant selector styles elements only when they appear inside a specific ancestor.
css-descendant-selector.objective: Use a descendant selector to set color on only the li elements inside .feature-list.
hints: A space between two selectors means "inside". It narrows a rule to one area of the page.
Write .feature-list followed by a space and li, then set color.
`.feature-list li { color: #0f766e; }`
checks: Feature list items are targeted by context

css-padding.title: Add internal space
css-padding.summary: padding creates space between an element border and its content.
css-padding.objective: Add padding to .preview-card so card content moves away from the visible card edge.
hints: Padding is the space inside an element, between its content and its edge.
Target .preview-card and set padding to a length.
`.preview-card { padding: 1.25rem; }`

css-margin.title: Separate page sections
css-margin.summary: margin creates space outside an element.
css-margin.objective: Add margin to .content-shell so sections are separated from nearby content.
hints: Margin is the space outside an element. It pushes other content away.
Target .content-shell and set margin. A value like 2rem auto adds space above and below.
`.content-shell { margin: 2rem auto; }`

css-border.title: Draw a component boundary
css-border.summary: The border shorthand sets width, style, and color in one declaration.
hints: A border needs a width, a style, and a color. The shorthand sets all three at once.
Target .preview-card and set border with a width, solid, and a color.
`.preview-card { border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; }`
checks: Preview cards have a solid border

css-border-color.title: Outline the featured card
css-border-color.summary: Border color can highlight a component without changing its content.
css-border-color.objective: Target .featured-card and set border-color. The card already has a transparent border in the preview.
hints: When an element already has a border, you can change just one part of it.
Target .featured-card and set only border-color. The width and style are already there.
`.featured-card { border-color: #2563eb; }`
checks: Featured card has a border color

css-radius.title: Soften component corners
css-radius.summary: border-radius rounds box corners and is common for cards, inputs, and buttons.
css-radius.objective: Set border-radius on .preview-card. The preview already gives cards a visible surface and border.
hints: Rounded corners come from one property applied to the edge of the element.
Target .preview-card and set border-radius to a length.
`.preview-card { border-radius: 0.75rem; }`

css-shadow.title: Lift cards from the page
css-shadow.summary: box-shadow creates depth when used subtly.
css-shadow.objective: Add box-shadow to the visible .preview-card surfaces.
hints: A shadow adds depth. It needs offsets, a blur, and a color.
Target .preview-card and set box-shadow with a soft, transparent color.
`.preview-card { box-shadow: 0 16px 30px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.14); }`

css-max-width.title: Constrain reading width
css-max-width.summary: max-width keeps long content readable on wide screens. Auto side margins center fixed-width blocks.
css-max-width.objective: Set max-width on .content-shell and center it with margin.
hints: Very long lines are hard to read. Limit the width, then center the block.
On .content-shell, set max-width, then use margin with auto on the left and right.
`.content-shell { max-width: 72rem; margin: 2rem auto; }`
checks: Content shell has a max width
Content shell is centered with margin

css-display-flex.title: Turn tools into a row
css-display-flex.summary: Flexbox arranges children along one axis and is ideal for toolbars.
hints: Flexbox lines up the children of an element in a row.
Target .toolbar and change its display value.
`.toolbar { display: flex; }`

css-gap.title: Space flex children
css-gap.summary: gap creates consistent space between flex or grid children.
hints: Flex items touch by default. One property adds even space between them.
Target .toolbar and set gap to a length.
`.toolbar { gap: 0.75rem; }`

css-justify-content.title: Distribute toolbar actions
css-justify-content.summary: justify-content controls spacing along the main flex axis.
css-justify-content.objective: Use justify-content on the flex .toolbar to distribute its children.
hints: In a flex row, the free space can be shared out in different ways.
Target .toolbar and set justify-content to space-between, center, or flex-end.
`.toolbar { justify-content: space-between; }`

css-nav-list.title: Make navigation horizontal
css-nav-list.summary: Navigation lists are still lists in HTML, but CSS controls their visual layout.
css-nav-list.objective: Remove bullets from .nav-list and make it a flex row.
hints: Navigation is often a list styled as a row: no bullets, items side by side.
On .nav-list, remove the bullets with list-style, then make it a flex container.
`.nav-list { list-style: none; display: flex; }`

css-card-grid.title: Create a card grid
css-card-grid.summary: CSS Grid arranges content in rows and columns.
hints: Grid places children in rows and columns. Like flexbox, it starts with the display property.
Target .card-grid and set display to grid.
`.card-grid { display: grid; }`

css-grid-columns.title: Define card columns
css-grid-columns.summary: grid-template-columns defines the column tracks in a grid.
css-grid-columns.objective: Set grid-template-columns on the grid .card-grid using repeat().
hints: A grid needs to know how many columns to create and how wide they are.
Set grid-template-columns on .card-grid. repeat() saves you from writing the same size several times.
`.card-grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); }`

css-pricing-grid.title: Lay out pricing cards
css-pricing-grid.summary: A grid container plus gap is the foundation for repeated card layouts.
css-pricing-grid.objective: Set display: grid and gap on .pricing-grid.
hints: Practice both steps of a grid at once: create it, then space its items.
In one .pricing-grid rule, set display to grid and add gap.
`.pricing-grid { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }`

css-pricing-card.title: Build a reusable card rule
css-pricing-card.summary: Reusable component classes let repeated markup share the same visual treatment.
hints: A component is a few properties working together. Combine inner space and an edge.
In one .pricing-card rule, set padding and border.
`.pricing-card { padding: 1rem; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; }`
checks: Pricing card has padding and border

css-link-button.title: Make a link feel actionable
css-link-button.summary: Links can be styled as buttons while keeping anchor semantics.
css-link-button.objective: Style .cta-button with display: inline-block and remove text-decoration.
hints: Links are inline and underlined. Looking like a button means changing both.
On .cta-button, set display to inline-block and text-decoration to none.
`.cta-button { display: inline-block; text-decoration: none; }`
checks: Call-to-action behaves like a button box

css-hover-state.title: Add a hover state
css-hover-state.summary: Pseudo-classes style interactive states without changing the HTML.
css-hover-state.objective: Create a .cta-button:hover rule that changes background-color.
hints: A pseudo-class applies styles only in a certain state, like when the pointer is over an element.
Write a .cta-button:hover rule and change background-color inside it.
`.cta-button:hover { background-color: #1d4ed8; }`

css-focus-state.title: Show keyboard focus
css-focus-state.summary: Focus styles help keyboard users see which control is active.
css-focus-state.objective: Create a .field:focus rule with an outline.
hints: Keyboard users need to see which field is active. The focus state exists for that.
Write a .field:focus rule and set an outline.
`.field:focus { outline: 3px solid #2563eb; }`

css-custom-property.title: Define a reusable color
css-custom-property.summary: Custom properties store reusable values that can be referenced elsewhere with var().
hints: Custom properties store a value once so you can reuse it everywhere. Their names start with two hyphens.
In a :root rule, declare --accent with a color.
`:root { --accent: #2563eb; }`
checks: Root defines an accent custom property

css-use-variable.title: Use a custom property
css-use-variable.summary: var() reads a custom property so related components can share a design token.
hints: A stored value is read back with a function that takes the custom property name.
On .cta-button, set background-color using var() with --accent inside.
`.cta-button { background-color: var(--accent); }`

css-transition.title: Smooth state changes
css-transition.summary: transition smooths property changes such as hover colors.
css-transition.objective: Add transition to .cta-button so its existing hover color change animates.
hints: A transition animates the change between two states instead of jumping.
Add transition to .cta-button itself, not to the hover rule, with a property and a duration.
`.cta-button { transition: background-color 180ms ease; }`

css-nth-child.title: Style one repeated item
css-nth-child.summary: Structural pseudo-classes target elements based on their position among siblings.
css-nth-child.objective: Use .timeline-item:nth-child(2) to style the second timeline item.
hints: Some pseudo-classes pick elements by their position among their siblings.
Write .timeline-item:nth-child(2) and set background-color.
`.timeline-item:nth-child(2) { background-color: #dbeafe; }`
checks: Second timeline item has a targeted style

css-table-stripes.title: Stripe table rows
css-table-stripes.summary: Structural selectors are useful for repeated data, such as table rows.
css-table-stripes.objective: Use .metrics-table tr:nth-child(even) to set a background-color.
hints: nth-child also accepts keywords, so one rule can style every other row.
Target .metrics-table tr:nth-child(even) and set background-color.
`.metrics-table tr:nth-child(even) { background-color: #f1f5f9; }`
checks: Even metric rows have a background color

css-pseudo-element.title: Add generated decoration
css-pseudo-element.summary: Pseudo-elements create style-only pieces of a component without changing HTML.
hints: Pseudo-elements add decoration that is not in the HTML. They only appear when they have content.
Write a .quote::before rule with a content declaration.
`.quote::before { content: "“"; }`

css-sticky-header.title: Keep navigation visible
css-sticky-header.summary: position: sticky keeps an element in normal flow until it reaches an offset.
css-sticky-header.objective: Make .site-header sticky and pin it to the top.
hints: A sticky element scrolls normally until it reaches an edge, then stays there.
On .site-header, set position to sticky and top to 0.
`.site-header { position: sticky; top: 0; }`
checks: Site header is sticky at the top

css-absolute-badge.title: Place a badge inside a card
css-absolute-badge.summary: Absolute children position against the nearest positioned ancestor.
css-absolute-badge.objective: Make .featured-card position: relative and .badge position: absolute.
hints: An absolute element is placed relative to its closest positioned parent.
Make .featured-card position: relative, then make .badge position: absolute with top and right.
`.featured-card { position: relative; }` and `.badge { position: absolute; top: 1rem; right: 1rem; }`
checks: Featured card creates a positioning context

css-media-card-grid.title: Stack cards on small screens
css-media-card-grid.summary: Media queries let layout respond to viewport width.
css-media-card-grid.objective: Inside a max-width media query, set the existing .card-grid columns to 1fr.
hints: Media queries apply rules only when the screen matches a condition, like a small width.
Write @media (max-width: 700px) and put a .card-grid rule inside it.
`@media (max-width: 700px) { .card-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; } }`
checks: Small-screen media query stacks the card grid

css-media-nav.title: Reflow navigation
css-media-nav.summary: Responsive navigation often changes direction when horizontal space is limited.
css-media-nav.objective: Inside a max-width media query, set the existing .nav-list flex-direction to column.
hints: On narrow screens, a row of links often fits better as a column.
Inside a max-width media query, set flex-direction on .nav-list.
`@media (max-width: 700px) { .nav-list { flex-direction: column; } }`
checks: Small-screen media query stacks navigation links

css-keyframes.title: Define a small animation
css-keyframes.summary: @keyframes defines animation steps; animation applies them to an element.
css-keyframes.objective: Create @keyframes pulse and use animation on .badge.
hints: An animation has two parts: keyframes that describe the change, and a property that plays them.
Define @keyframes pulse with from and to steps, then set animation on .badge using the name pulse.
`@keyframes pulse { from { opacity: 0.65; } to { opacity: 1; } }` and `.badge { animation: pulse 1s infinite alternate; }`

css-reduced-motion.title: Respect motion preferences
css-reduced-motion.summary: prefers-reduced-motion lets users avoid unnecessary animation.
css-reduced-motion.objective: Inside a prefers-reduced-motion media query, set .badge animation to none.
hints: Some people feel unwell with motion on screen. Their system can ask websites to reduce it.
Write @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and turn off the .badge animation inside it.
`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .badge { animation: none; } }`
checks: Reduced-motion media query disables badge animation

css-capstone.title: Style the preview page
css-capstone.summary: A complete CSS pass combines reusable values, layout rules, component styles, states, and responsive behavior.
css-capstone.objective: Combine variables, layout, cards, hover state, and a responsive media query to style the fixed preview page.
hints: Work through one requirement at a time and watch the checklist. Start with the variable.
Define --accent on :root, center .lab-page, make .card-grid a grid, add a hover rule, and finish with a max-width media query.
Reuse what you learned: `:root { --accent: #2563eb; }`, `.card-grid { display: grid; }`, a `:hover` rule, and `@media (max-width: 700px) { ... }`.
checks: Lab page is centered with a max width
Card grid uses columns and gap
